hook: In most games, the economy is a spreadsheet. Prices never move. Nobody is really trading. Nims is a town where every merchant is an AI agent, with its own money and its own mind about prices.
signin: You sign in with an email. That's all. No wallet, no seed phrase, no gas: the game makes your account and pays every fee behind the scenes.
goal: Pick a goal. Nim, your guide, always says what to do next.
collect: Buy cotton at the wholesaler, then carry it to a stall that pays more.
tooltip: Every price has a reason. Hover it, and the merchant explains in plain words: how much stock they hold, who sold to them this hour, and what they can afford.
sale: Sell, and the cash lands instantly. The game never waits for a block.
order: Too far to walk? Place a delivery order: the goods, and the lowest price you'll take. The town's carriers wait for that price, then sell the load for you.
filled: And there it is. Sold, with no walking.
prices: The price board shows every good in every market, against its usual price.
shares: You can even own a piece of a merchant, and earn a share of their profit each evening.
sim: Because every merchant reacts to the others, one trader flooding the market crashes a price for everyone. No scripted event. No developer patch. That is the economy as the gameplay.
chain: And it's all real. Every good is a token on NEAR testnet, settled in batches by a relayer, so you never see a wallet. Here is the live contract.
outro: Nims. Agent merchants. Email login. NEP-245 goods. Delivery orders in the spirit of NEAR Intents. The economy is the game.
